cards.card_text: Moses says one lone witness isn't enough to prove a man did wrong, no matter what the offense is.
cards.verse_text: A lone witness is not sufficient to establish any wrongdoing or sin against a man, regardless of what offense he may have committed.
cards.snippet: …to establish any wrongdoing or sin against a man, regardless of what offense he may have committed.

cards.card_text: She asks him to forgive her offense.
cards.verse_text: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles.

cards.card_text: Now somebody's committed an offense, and Solomon says there are two ways to handle it, but only one of them promotes love.
cards.verse_text: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
cards.snippet: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.

cards.card_text: If the ruler's temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for ___ lays great offenses to rest.
cards.verse_text: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
cards.snippet: …flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.

cards.card_text: And when the people ask, "For what offense has the LORD our God done all these things to us?" the LORD has an answer ready.
cards.verse_text: And when the people ask, ‘For what offense has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ You are to tell them, ‘Just as you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.’”

cards.card_text: And if he were, Paul says, "In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished."

cards.card_text: Then Peter quotes one more Scripture about this stone, from Isaiah again (Isa 8:14): “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.”
cards.verse_text: and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.
